### Spec build

**You own the ticket graph and the spec branch, never a ticket's code. Run every ready ticket at once, land each one on the spec branch, review once at the end.** For a spec that splits into several tickets with blocking edges, some able to build in parallel, built in one session and delivered as one PR ("build this spec", "implement all the tickets", "run the tickets in parallel"). One coupled change goes to Feature with one owner. A spec too large to review as one PR goes to Autopilot-stack. Work that outlives one session goes to Orchestrate.

**Before step 1.** Open the worktree per the **Worktree** section of `SKILL.md`. The worktree holds the spec branch and every landed ticket. The intent and the tickets file stay at the root, per the **nstack folder** section of `SKILL.md`. You run git and verify commands in it and edit no code there, except for the `/no-comments` and `/simplify` passes that SKILL.md runs before review and Opening a PR runs before the PR. Commit what they change. The Interview round drafts the ticket graph with the user and confirms it with the design.

1. **Write the tickets file.** Write the confirmed graph to `<root>/.nstack/intents/<slug>-tickets.md`. The intent names this path instead of restating the graph. One section per ticket, numbered in dependency order, each with these lines.
   - **Builds.** The behavior the ticket makes work, seen from the user's side. A vertical slice through every layer it needs, sized to one fresh context window.
   - **Blocked by.** The ticket numbers that gate it, or `None`.
   - **Writes.** The paths or globs it may write.
   - **Acceptance.** Checkable criteria, one per line.
   - **Verify.** The exact command. Mark it `root-only` when it reads gitignored fixtures, a local database, or credentials a worktree lacks.

   Prefactoring is its own ticket and blocks the rest. When tickets on both sides of a process boundary (client and server, two services) share a message or data shape, that shape is its own ticket and both sides block on it. Two tickets whose **Writes** overlap get a blocking edge, or the file pins the exact names each one adds (catalogue keys, types, registry entries). A worktree does not remove a collision. It moves the collision to merge time. When a ticket splits, gains an edge, or is abandoned, amend this file in the same run.
2. **Track each ticket's state.** Keep one todo per ticket in one of four states: blocked, in flight, landed, abandoned. A ticket is landed only when `git log <spec-branch> --grep='^Ticket: <NN>$'` finds a commit. Confirm landings there, never from memory or tracker state. A tracker counts a blocker done only when it closes, which is the end of the run. The frontier is every blocked ticket whose blockers have all landed.
3. **Explore once, when the tickets need it.** One `nstack:n-agent` at `effort: "medium"` reads the code and docs the tickets touch and writes notes to a directory outside the repo that its brief names. The notes hold file pointers, conventions, and test commands. Every brief points at them, so implementers build instead of re-exploring. Skip this step when the tickets already name everything.
4. **Spawn the frontier.** Spawn frontier tickets in one message, at most eight in flight, and mark each one in flight. One `nstack:n-agent` per ticket, `isolation: "worktree"`, on the code model at the implementation effort for that model, per the **Subagents** section. The brief holds pointers, not pasted context: the absolute paths of the intent and the tickets file, the ticket number, the explore notes, the spec branch, and the ticket branch `<spec-branch>--t<NN>`. It tells the implementer to:
   - start with `git branch -m <ticket-branch>` and `git reset --hard <spec-branch>`, so the branch has a known name and starts at the spec tip whatever its worktree was cut from;
   - write the failing test first when the ticket has a cheap local test target, per **principle-test-behavior-not-implementation**, or report `test-first skipped: <reason>`;
   - write only inside the ticket's **Writes**, and report anything outside it as a follow-up instead of fixing it;
   - end every commit message with a `Ticket: <NN>` trailer;
   - run **Verify**, and report a `root-only` check as unrun, never as green;
   - rebase onto the current spec tip, re-run **Verify**, and report the branch, the head SHA, each command with its result, and every deviation.
5. **Land one completion at a time.** Finish a landing before you read the next completion. Every command here runs in the spec worktree.
   - Read the diff against the ticket's **Writes** and **Acceptance**.
   - Run `git switch --detach <spec-branch>`, then `git merge --ff-only <ticket-branch>`. When another ticket landed first and the fast-forward is refused, run `git cherry-pick HEAD..<ticket-branch>` instead. On a conflict, run `git cherry-pick --abort` and `git switch <spec-branch>`, then spawn a fresh `nstack:n-agent` at the implementation effort with `isolation: "worktree"` to replay the ticket's commits onto the spec tip on branch `<ticket-branch>-replay`, resolving inside the ticket's slice. Land that branch the same way. Never resume the finished implementer.
   - Run the ticket's **Verify** yourself on the detached head. For a `root-only` check, first copy in the gitignored files it reads from the root checkout.
   - Green, note the head SHA, run `git switch <spec-branch>` and `git merge --ff-only <that SHA>`, and mark the ticket landed. Red, run `git switch <spec-branch>` and send the ticket to step 6's retry. The spec branch moves only after a green **Verify**, so an implementer that rebases mid-landing never picks up an unverified commit.
6. **Refill or retry after every landing.** Recompute the frontier and spawn what fits under the cap. Retry a failed ticket once, with the failure in the brief, on branch `<spec-branch>--t<NN>-retry`, because the first attempt's worktree still holds the original branch. A second failure abandons that ticket and every ticket that depends on it, directly or through other tickets. Never build a dependent on a guess.
7. **Review once, when nothing is in flight and the frontier is empty.** Every ticket is then landed or abandoned. Never review mid-run. A review against the spec reads every unbuilt ticket as a failure and starts building it.
   - Run the full test suite and the typecheck once in the spec worktree.
   - Run Claude Code's built-in `/code-review` over `<integration>...<spec-branch>`.
   - Spawn a `nstack:n-agent` on the final branch review's model and effort, per the **Subagents** section, to check the branch against the intent and the **Acceptance** of every landed ticket. Name the abandoned tickets so it does not build them. It reads the diff and distrusts the reports.

   Give every finding to one fresh `nstack:n-agent` at the implementation effort with `isolation: "worktree"`. It starts like a ticket on branch `<spec-branch>--fix`, takes the findings as its acceptance criteria, and skips the **Writes** bound and the `Ticket:` trailer. Its **Verify** is the full suite and the typecheck from the first bullet. Land it per step 5. A red landing gets one more fresh fix implementer on `<spec-branch>--fix-retry`, and a second red ends the review with those findings reported as unfixed. Then re-check only the findings it fixed. Do not start a second broad review. Anything new goes in the PR body as a follow-up.
8. **Verify on the live surface.** Verify the spec branch on the matching surface, as Feature step 5 does. A green suite does not replace it.
9. Run **Opening a PR** for the spec branch. One PR is deliberate here, because the review covered the tickets as one whole. When it tidies the history, keep each ticket's commits together, in landing order, with their `Ticket:` trailers. When the merge-back in the **Worktree** section must rebase the spec branch and the rebase conflicts, run `git rebase --abort` and spawn a fresh `nstack:n-agent` at `effort: "high"` with no isolation, which works in the spec worktree, to redo the rebase, resolve it, and re-run the full suite. After the merge-back returns you to the root, remove every ticket worktree that `git worktree list` shows with `git worktree remove --force`. Then delete each branch that `git branch --list '<spec-branch>--*'` prints, one `git branch -D` per name.

**Reply:** the ticket graph with each ticket's state, the peak number of tickets in flight, what the review found and what the fix landed, abandoned tickets and why, follow-ups, and the PR link.
